candidateSources.sourceLocator: PDF page 23 (printed "Version 2 EE IIT, Kharagpur 23"); section "4.7 The Triac / 4.7.1 Construction and operating principle"
candidateSources.retrievedPassage: The Triac is a member of the thyristor family. But unlike a thyristor which conducts only in one direction (from anode to cathode) a triac can conduct in both directions. Thus a triac is similar to two back to back (anti parallel) connected thyristors but with only three terminals. As in the case of a thyristor, the conduction of a triac is initiated by injecting a current pulse into the gate terminal. The gate looses control over conduction once the triac is turned on. The triac turns off only when the current through the main terminals become zero. Therefore, a triac can be categorized as a minority carrier, a bidirectional semi-controlled device.

normalizedClaims.claimText: A TRIAC's basic operating principle: it is a bidirectional (both-direction-conducting) member of the thyristor family, functionally similar to two anti-parallel thyristors sharing three terminals; conduction is initiated by a gate current pulse, and once conducting the gate loses control -- the TRIAC only turns off when current through the main terminals falls to zero.
